structure.title: Challenging the model of womanhood
structure.text: Early chapters attack accounts that make dependence and pleasing manners women's proper destination.

structure.title: Education and shared responsibility
structure.text: Later chapters connect rational education with marriage, parenting, citizenship, and the possibility of independent judgment.

people.name: Reason
people.text: The faculty Wollstonecraft argues women have as fully as men, and which their education trains them to neglect in favour of charm.

people.name: Virtue
people.text: Goodness founded on understanding rather than obedience, which Wollstonecraft insists must mean the same thing for women as for men.

people.name: Dependence
people.text: The condition of women kept reliant on men for money, status and approval, which Wollstonecraft argues makes them weak, not virtuous.

context.title: Education creates evidence
context.text: Wollstonecraft challenges the circular argument that trained dependence proves natural incapacity. Social formation becomes part of the explanation.
context.takeaway: Ask how the observed character was produced.

context.title: Equality and obligation
context.text: Equal moral standing brings demands for responsible conduct, not merely access to admiration or comfort. Her criticism addresses women as well as men.

notice.why: Praise can reward the conduct that maintains dependence.
Private relationships reveal the consequences of unequal education.

opening: Girls are trained to be pleasing, dependent, and preoccupied with appearance. Then men cite those qualities as evidence that women are naturally unfit for independence. Mary Wollstonecraft attacks the arrangement at its source: an education designed to make obedience attractive and reason unnecessary. Her argument makes demands on women as well as men, insisting that dignity involves developing judgment and accepting responsibility. The force of this early feminist work comes from refusing the compliments that help keep a person permanently in someone else's care.
